purpose: Dashboard design exploration; all values are illustrative demo data.

concepts.title: Dark energy
concepts.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Asset type: high-fidelity desktop web application design proposal for ThermaVoltFlow, intended for later implementation with Svelte frontend and PHP backend. Generate ONE complete flat front-facing dashboard screenshot, wide landscape 16:10 canvas, crisp readable English UI typography and professional spacing. No browser chrome, no laptop frame, no presentation border, no watermark. This is an interface design, not a poster.
Product requirements: THREE INDEPENDENT energy systems: Home electricity, Water heating, EV charging. Each has its OWN dedicated solar installation and its OWN source selector: "Solar", "Grid", "Off", "Schedule". A shared utility company connection is the fallback source, with separately controlled branches to each system. Do not imply one solar array supplies all three. No battery storage, wind turbines, or extra systems.
Show attractive actual 3D rendered assets: a modern home and its solar panels, a separate solar installation paired with a hot-water tank, and a separate solar canopy paired with an electric car and visible wall charger. Energy paths use fine directional arrows and spaced bright particles to communicate the intended later animation. This is a static preview of flowing energy. Render recognizably different physical assets, beautiful restrained materials, precise contact shadows.
Navigation exact labels: "Dashboard", "Control Center", "Smart Scheduler", "Analytics". Brand exact spelling: "ThermaVoltFlow". Page heading: "Energy overview"; small badge "DEMO DATA".
Numbers must be legible and plausible: current solar power "7.3 kW", home consumption "2.6 kW", water consumption "1.5 kW", EV consumption "3.2 kW", grid import "0.0 kW". All three system cards show Solar selected, with all four source options visible. Water temperature "54°C"; EV battery "68%". Do not confuse kW and kWh.
Essential: substantial real charts with labeled time axes and units, including a 24-hour solar-versus-grid power history chart ("Power · kW", ticks 00, 06, 12, 18, 24) and compact daily energy statistics "Solar today 28.4 kWh", "Used today 34.8 kWh", "Exported today 0.0 kWh". Include a visibly editable schedule preview with different source blocks, for example "Tomorrow · Home", Grid 00–07, Solar 07–17, Grid 17–24. Scheduling can independently assign each subsystem to solar, grid, or off at different hours.
Include a clearly labeled separate "Export surplus" control with switch visibly OFF, helper "Send surplus solar energy to the grid", and "User opt-in". Export is an optional setting and should not be shown as active or paying money. Do not make claims about feed-in tariffs.
Keep hierarchy calm and buildable, avoid tiny text or dense unreadable micro widgets. Exact important UI labels over decorative text.
Style direction A: an elegant dark energy command dashboard. Charcoal backgrounds, restrained emerald energy traces, white text and muted gray metadata, warm amber grid identity. Narrow left navigation rail with the brand and four labeled links. Main content: header and an understated row of three large numeric KPIs; then an expansive central 3D ecosystem stage, with three distinct dedicated solar-device clusters on one dark floor plane. Keep the three clusters visibly independent with clear labels Home, Water, EV and their own energy traces. To the right of the stage, a clear vertical control column with three source selectors, temperatures and charge percentage, and Export surplus off. The lower third devotes substantial width to the solar/grid history area chart and an independent compact schedule preview. The 3D centerpiece must be prominent, with a beautiful miniature modern house, slate solar cells, silver cylinder, ivory car and charger. Avoid neon sci-fi HUDs, excessive bloom, holograms, and extraneous decorative rings. Professional production UI, strong typographic scale.

Style direction B: airy warm white product dashboard, approachable and refined. Off-white page, crisp white surfaces, charcoal typography, fresh green energy identity, orange for heating details and blue for grid labels. Horizontal top navigation with brand at left and four links, Dashboard active. Large clear title followed by a restrained text-based metrics strip. Main hero is THREE EQUAL LARGE SIDE-BY-SIDE SYSTEM PANELS occupying the middle of the dashboard: Home electricity, Water heating, EV charging. Each panel includes its own beautiful miniature clay-and-realistic hybrid 3D vignette of its dedicated solar panels and device, directional energy paths, large live kW number, and its own four-option segmented source selector with Solar selected. Distinct independent systems are immediately obvious. Very thin borders, generous space, restrained corner radius and only gentle shadows. Below, a wide easy-to-read two-series power chart occupies about two thirds, while the remainder holds an elegant schedule preview and the explicit Export surplus OFF switch. Small daily kWh stats above the chart. Make all sections fit without truncation. This concept should feel visually different from a dark mission-control screen, with 3D objects and clean reading as the main experience.

Style direction C: precision engineering dashboard with a cool midnight navy navigation sidebar, light icy-gray analytical workspace, cyan/teal solar paths and amber grid indications. A more structured layout with compact square-ish cards and hairline dividers; beautiful monospaced numeric readings alongside refined sans-serif labels. Left navigation clearly includes all four pages. Across the top a horizontal power-balance strip displays solar generation 7.3 kW, loads 7.3 kW, grid import 0.0 kW and export 0.0 kW.
Dominant upper main region is a rigorous but attractive 3D isometric topology on a subtle drafting grid: three separate solar-to-load branches in three lanes, each with a miniature dedicated PV array, one house / hot-water tank / EV plus charger respectively, clear arrows and a 2.6 / 1.5 / 3.2 kW reading. A utility meter along one edge has thin inactive dashed fallback branches to each load, never connecting the three solar arrays together. Put the three independent four-way source selectors in a neat column next to the topology. Visual topology must remain readable and not become spaghetti. The lower main region has a large labeled solar/grid history chart and a full-width clean mixed-source schedule lane beneath it. Daily kWh stats clearly visible. Place Export surplus OFF in a dedicated footer control with the opt-in helper. This design balances the requested 3D physical objects with high-priority charts and numerical readings, feeling like a premium engineering instrument with a light readable content area. No fake code or terminal text.
